entries.english:
(Co-)Plaintiff/applicant/intervenor: Albrecht von Dienheim zu Dexheim.
(Co-)Defendant/intervenor: the male-fief heirs of Albrecht von Rosenberg, namely Konrad von Vellberg zu Vellberg and Leofels; Hans von Steinau called Steinrück, Würzburg princely-bishopric official at Trimberg; and Philipp Geyer von Giebelstadt, guardians of Zaisolf von Rosenberg's minor sons Albrecht Christoph and Georg Sigmund von Rosenberg; their brother Konrad von Rosenberg zu Gnötzheim; and Hans Christoph von Rosenberg zu Rosenberg and Essingen.

The case concerns a dispute over possession of fief property. In March 1581 Dienheim unsuccessfully asked the male-fief heirs to initiate an arbitral procedure over allodial and hereditary fief properties he had bought but which they withheld. In September 1581, and again in April 1582 when some heirs and guardians initially remained unnamed, he summoned them before the Imperial Chamber Court. He sought delivery of the allodial properties and Würzburg princely-bishopric and Hohenlohe comital hereditary fiefs sold to him, including the patronage of Buch parish, 17 Malter of protection oats at Dainbach, 8 Eimer of rent wine from 15 Morgen of vineyards at Sachsenflur, meadows and woods at Dainbach and Sachsenflur, mills at Sachsenflur and Unterschüpf, and vineyards at Ober- and Unterschüpf, as well as division of the previously shared rights, jurisdictions, and serfs. The defendants denied that these goods and dues had been sold to Dienheim and argued that some could not be alienated as male fiefs: the patronage of Buch belonged with the whole village to Wertheim as a male fief; the Boxberg Palatinate office had taken the protection oats, meadows, and woods, later granting them as Palatinate male fiefs to Albrecht von Rosenberg, who improperly assigned the oats to Unterschüpf Castle; Oberschüpf and its vineyards were half Mainz male fief; and the Unterschüpf vineyards were Wertheim male fief. Dienheim should pursue the allodial heirs, with whom he was already disputing the allegedly unsold half of lordship, fishing, and hunting rights at Unterschüpf.

Proceedings: Imperial Chamber Court 1582–1588 (recorded as 1582–1589).

Included documents: the 1578 purchase agreement between Albrecht von Rosenberg's allodial heirs and Albrecht von Dienheim; the 1577 agreement between his male-fief and allodial heirs concerning Mainz fiefs; the 1579 settlement and partition agreement concerning the inherited male and hereditary fiefs and allodial property; and Archbishop Daniel of Mainz's 1557 authorization for the exchange of the patronages of Assamstadt and Buch between Abbot Theobald of Amorbach and Albrecht von Rosenberg.

Contents/inserted notes: Register of the beginning of proceedings: 1582.
